categories.main_business_segments: Corteva operates through two primary business segments: Seed and Crop Protection. The Seed segment develops and supplies advanced germplasm and trait technologies for crops such as corn, soybeans, and other oilseeds, while the Crop Protection segment provides products that protect crops from weeds, insects, and diseases, including herbicides, insecticides, fungicides, and nitrogen stabilizers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Corteva leverages advanced breeding technologies, biotechnology traits, and digital agronomy tools to develop high-yield seeds and crop protection products. The company utilizes proprietary germplasm, gene editing, precision agriculture, and large-scale data analytics, as well as fermentation and chemical synthesis for crop protection active ingredients. Production involves both company-owned facilities and third-party contract manufacturers and growers.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Corteva primarily serves farmers and agricultural producers globally, as well as distributors, cooperatives, and dealers. Its key end markets are the global agriculture sector, focusing on row crops such as corn, soybeans, canola, sunflower, and cotton, as well as specialty and horticultural crops.
categories.geographic_coverage: Corteva operates in approximately 140 countries, with significant sales in North America, EMEA (Europe, Middle East, and Africa), Latin America, and Asia Pacific. North America and Latin America are particularly important markets, with manufacturing and R&D facilities distributed globally.
categories.supply_chain_position: Corteva operates primarily as an upstream and midstream supplier in the agricultural value chain, providing seeds, traits, and crop protection products to farmers and agricultural distributors. The company sources raw materials and contracts with growers and manufacturers, positioning itself as a key input provider to the global food supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Corteva's strategic priorities include accelerating performance through portfolio simplification, achieving royalty neutrality, improving product mix with differentiated technologies, and driving operational improvements. The company invests heavily in R&D, focusing on innovation in seed traits, crop protection chemistry, biologicals, and digital agriculture solutions, with an emphasis on sustainability, climate resilience, and food security.
categories.revenue_model: Corteva generates revenue primarily through the sale of proprietary seeds, crop protection chemicals, and licensing of intellectual property. Revenue is also derived from royalties, digital agronomy services, and out-licensing of traits and germplasm to third parties.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Corteva competes globally with major agricultural input companies such as BASF, Bayer, FMC, Syngenta (ChemChina), as well as regional seed companies and generic crop protection producers. The company is positioned as a leading provider of integrated seed and crop protection solutions, with one of the broadest portfolios and innovation pipelines in the industry.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Corteva reported net sales of $17.5 billion, representing 11% year-over-year growth, with operating EBITDA of $3.2 billion. The company has demonstrated consistent revenue and earnings growth since its separation from DowDuPont in 2019, supported by strong price execution, volume gains, and productivity initiatives. Corteva maintains a robust balance sheet, investment-grade credit ratings, and significant liquidity.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Corteva differentiates itself through its science-based innovation, broad and productive product pipeline, and integrated solutions that enhance farmer productivity, profitability, and sustainability. The company emphasizes direct engagement with farmers, proprietary germplasm and trait technologies, and a unique multi-channel distribution model, delivering tailored solutions to address evolving agricultural challenges and regulatory requirements.
